verdict.justification: Deliverable B demonstrates much stronger financial modeling and logistical domain expertise. Because the analysis date in the environment was set in late 2026 (2026-11-05) while the prompt asks to project 2026 rates from 2020-2025 history, Deliverable B smartly retrieved the 2025 base published rates (`latest published price in effect at 31-Dec-2025`) to apply the estimated 2026 increase, while also including the actual 2026 published schedules in Table 3C and Table 6 to validate the projection. In contrast, Deliverable A applied the 2026 estimated rate increase on top of late-2026 holiday rates (`Rates were retrieved 2026-11-05 and already reflect 2026 carrier actions; as instructed, the 2020-2025 average increase is still applied`), effectively double-counting 2026 rate hikes and peak surcharges. Additionally, Deliverable B verified critical carrier program rules—confirming that for UPS Simple Rate `residential, delivery-area and fuel surcharges do not apply` and specifying the exact cubic-inch bands (`Medium (251-650 cu in)`)—whereas Deliverable A left surcharge rules unverified (`Not verified: whether UPS fuel or residential surcharges are added to Simple Rate`).
